Player Impressions:
Hoyos - Great game so far.  Has kept Atlanta in the game.  Saved a couple of shot from going in, including one from Báez.

Reilly - largely quiet.  He's being afforded a bit of space late in the half, and is able to mvoe the ball around.

Player Impressions:
Hoyos - Best performance of his time in Atlanta.  He kept Philadelphia from scoring 4 or 5 more
Alonso - was able to make a lot of clearances.  couldn't connect with those upfield
Jacob - looked outclassed, but still managed to defend good enough for most of the night.  Tired and beaten up
Báez - much better defensively in the 2nd half.  He wasn't asked to get forward, and was able to concentrate on only his defensive duties.
Muyumba - turned his attack up a notch in the 2nd half.  Wasn't trying to pass it, was trying to score.  Made some good runs, and that shot was wonderful
Reilly - He's not up to this level of play right now.  The game is a bit too fast for him.  He appears to be sinking rather than swimming.
Edwards - just able to hang on defensively.  couldn't get the ball up pitch.
Almirón - Trying to take the game on his terms.  Hard working on offense and defense.  Was knocked around hard all game, and gassed at the end.  Stumbled his way into an unexpected goal
Miranchuk - he's showing good numbers, passes well in pinball maneuvers.  Had trouble with his passes otherwise.  
Picault - Would be better as a AMC than a striker.  Is able to connect with others and pass.  Does press the back line, but cannot get a shot off.
Gregersen - came on late.  Made some good clearances.  
Brennan - Made a couple of runs, but not good enough.  Caused more havoc than helped
Kovac - should have been brought on earlier.  made some defensive plays.  ran around, but the game was long-ago set against Atlanta.  He wasn't able to see attacking balls
Hernández - made a couple of good clearances.  He and Edwards weren't on the same page.  He was beaten on his side.


Wagner and Sullivan were the best players for Philadelphia.  Sullivan is going to light up the prem.
